newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST--Japan Sept c/a surplus seen easing.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--Japan Sept c/a surplus seen easing.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus for September is expected to show a steady decline from the year-earlier period, and the pace of the drop will continue to slow in coming months, economists said on Thursday.

A Reuters poll of economists forecast the surplus in the current account -- the broadest measure of merchandise and services trade -- will have fallen to an average 860.7 billion yen in September from 1.13 trillion yen a year earlier. The forecasts ranged from 809 billion yen to 922.7 billion yen.
The September current account figures are due to be released at 0850 a.m. on Monday (2350 GMT Sunday) November 11.
"The extent and the pace of the decline are slowing down," said Tomoko Fujii, an economist at Salomon Brothers Asia Ltd.

She attributed the slowing pace mainly to the yen's weakness against the dollar which has helped exports rebound and capped growth in imports. "I expect the decline in the surplus to stop within this year and perhaps start rising slightly."

Other economists said the pace of the decline in the surplus may slow down, but the declining trend would not change. Shuji Shirota, an economist at Yamaichi Research, said currency movements would not stop the general trend of companies moving their production overseas.
The services deficit is expected to have widened in September from a year ago on an increase in the number of Japanese travelling abroad, economists said.
